q: In 1831, Joseph Henry and Michael Faraday independently discovered the methods of producing electric current from ____ field.
e: In 1831, Joseph Henry and Michael Faraday independently discovered the methods of producing electric current from magnetic field. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. Faraday's law: induced emf equals the rate of change of magnetic flux through the loop.

q: This current is called an induced current and the electromotive force (emf) which causes the induced current to flow is called an induced ____.
e: This current is called an induced current and the electromotive force (emf) which causes the induced current to flow is called an induced emf. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

q: Again, a ____ current flows through the second loop when the first loop carrying a current is moved abruptly towards or away from the second loop.
e: Again, a momentary current flows through the second loop when the first loop carrying a current is moved abruptly towards or away from the second loop. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. Current is moved abruptly towards or away from the second loop. momentary.

q: The magnetic flux density or magnetic induction B is the number of magnetic lines of force passing perpendicularly through a unit ____ of material.
e: The magnetic flux density or magnetic induction B is the number of magnetic lines of force passing perpendicularly through a unit area of material. Flux density B is magnetic lines through unit area perpendicular to the field. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane.

q: Magnetic flux density B is related to magnetic field strength (magnetic field intensity) H by $B = $ ____.
e: Magnetic flux density B is related to magnetic field strength (magnetic field intensity) H by B = µ H. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. Flux density B is magnetic lines through unit area perpendicular to the field.

q: where $\mu$ is the permeability of the medium in which the magnetic field ____.
e: where µ is the permeability of the medium in which the magnetic field exists. The permeability of the medium in which the magnetic field ____. exists. A nearby word in place of exists would name a different quantity.

q: The SI unit of magnetic flux density is ____ which is equivalent to weber per metre squared.
e: The SI unit of magnetic flux density is tesla (T) which is equivalent to weber per metre squared. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. Flux density B is magnetic lines through unit area perpendicular to the field.

q: Magnetic flux $\Phi_B$ is a measurement of the total magnetic lines of force which passes through a surface ____.
e: Magnetic flux PhiB is a measurement of the total magnetic lines of force which passes through a surface area. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. Total magnetic lines of force which passes through a surface ____. area.

q: If the magnetic field is uniform over a plane area A, the magnetic flux $\Phi_B$ passing through that area A is simply $\Phi_B = $ ____.
e: If the magnetic field is uniform over a plane area A, the magnetic flux PhiB passing through that area A is simply PhiB = BA cos θ. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. The relation in this line is PhiB = ____.

q: When the field is perpendicular to the surface area, $\theta = 0^\circ$. Hence, $\Phi_B = $ ____.
e: When the field is perpendicular to the surface area, θ = 0^°. Hence, PhiB = BA. The relation in this line is PhiB = ____. A nearby word in place of BA would name a different quantity.

q: When the field is parallel to the surface area, $\theta = 90^\circ$. Hence, $\Phi_B = $ ____.
e: When the field is parallel to the surface area, θ = 90^°. Hence, PhiB = 0. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. The relation in this line is PhiB = ____.

q: The SI unit of magnetic flux is the ____.
e: The SI unit of magnetic flux is the weber (Wb). Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. The SI unit of magnetic flux is the ____. weber (Wb).

q: The weber is named after the German physicist Wilhelm Eduard ____.
e: The weber is named after the German physicist Wilhelm Eduard Weber. The weber is named after the German physicist Wilhelm Eduard ____. Weber. A nearby word in place of Weber would name a different quantity.

q: Magnetic field strength and magnetic flux density are vector quantities whereas magnetic flux is a ____ quantity.
e: Magnetic field strength and magnetic flux density are vector quantities whereas magnetic flux is a scalar quantity. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. Flux density B is magnetic lines through unit area perpendicular to the field.
